new_statements.quote: 2.1.3. Tone. The Mambiloid languages are register tone languages, all appearing to have either three or four tones at the lexical level. The four tone systems are plausibly a development of an earlier three tone system, while the three tone systems constitute an innovation relative to two tone systems found in related languages outside Mambiloid, for example most Bantu languages (Connell 1997a). The different tones, at least in most Mambiloid languages also combine on one syllable to form a number of tone contours. Tone also operates grammatically in Mambiloid languages, with modifications in the tone of the verb indicating, among other functions, imperative mood and changes in tense.

new_statements.relation_note: Register tone, 3-4 lexical tones across Mambiloid; contours; grammatical tone. No stress/accent remark. Vowel and consonant sections exemplify Ba-Mambila and Sundani-Kwanja only.
new_statements.rule_in_words: All Mambiloid languages (Somyev listed among them) are register tone languages with three or four lexical tone levels, contour combinations on single syllables, and grammatical tone on verbs; nothing is said about stress or accent for any member language.
new_statements.exceptions: none; author stresses that 'the vast majority of these languages have not been studied at all' and generalizations may need 'substantial modification' (sec. 2, p. 84-85)
new_statements.identity_note: Group-level sketch of Mambiloid by the fieldworker who recorded Somyev; Somyev [kgt] is listed as a member language in Table One ('Kila Yang (20)' regional name / 'Somyev' own name) and mentioned individually for pluralization (je~w 'many') and a possible e- infinitive prefix. The tone statement is quantified over all Mambiloid languages, not made of Somyev by name.
